Times of Israel, 18 Nov 2026 18:58 (page time) — retrieved via WebFetch 21:20 GMT; the tool returned a point summary of the article rather than verbatim text, so this file is used for corroboration only, not for quotations

- The operation: On Wednesday, the Israeli military began a rare operation in central Gaza, beyond the Yellow Line that divides Israeli and Hamas-controlled areas. Its stated aim was to destroy a tunnel.
- Evacuation orders: COGAT, Israel's liaison body to the Palestinians, told residents of parts of the Bureij and Nuseirat areas to leave. Evacuation orders have been unusual since the October 2025 US-brokered ceasefire.
- Reported advances: Palestinian media reported Israeli tanks advancing in the area for the first time since the ceasefire. The IDF said troops were working to destroy a tunnel that posed an immediate threat to its forces.
- Related strikes: The IDF said it killed two Hamas platoon commanders in separate strikes in Khan Younis and Jabalia the previous day, accusing them of violating the ceasefire.
- Background: Under the ceasefire, Israel was to pull back to the Yellow Line, which left it controlling 53% of Gaza. Netanyahu later directed the IDF to expand its control to 70%.
- Ceasefire status: More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire took effect, according to Hamas-affiliated health officials. Five Israeli soldiers have been killed in the same period.
- Diplomatic warnings: The US-backed Board of Peace warned the UN Security Council that the ceasefire could collapse without full implementation. Hamas dismissed the report as "pure disinformation."
